hints.content:
We are given the lengths of two sides, $\goldE{\overline{PQ}}$ and $\maroonD{\overline{QR}}$:

- $\goldE{\overline{PQ}}$ is the side adjacent to the angle whose measure we want to find, $\angle Q$.
- $\maroonD{\overline{QR}}$ is the hypotenuse since it is across from the right angle.



[[☃ image 1]]

We can use the ratio of these side lengths to approximate $m\angle Q$.

options.alt: Triangle P Q R. Side P Q is two point five units. Angle P is a right angle. Angle Q is the angle of reference. Side Q R is four point four units. A dashed arrow points from angle P to side Q R.

hints.content:
We need to relate the adjacent side to the hypotenuse.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{\text{adjacent leg length}}{\text{hypotenuse length}} &= \dfrac{PQ}{QR}\\\\
&\approx \dfrac{2.5}{4.4}\\\\
&\approx 0.57
\end{align}$

Let's find the ratio nearest to $0.57$ in the $\purpleD{\dfrac{\text{adjacent leg length}}{\text{hypotenuse length}}}$ row.

Angle | $\purpleD{55\degree}$ | $65\degree$ | $75\degree$
:-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
$\dfrac{\text{adjacent leg length}}{\text{hypotenuse length}}$ | $\boxed{\purpleD{0.57}}$ | $0.42$ | $0.26$

The nearest ratio value is in the $\purpleD{55\degree}$ column. So $55\degree$ is a pretty good estimate for $m\angle Q$.
The best estimate for $m\angle Q$ is $55\degree$.

question.content:
Given the measure of an acute angle in a right triangle, we can tell the ratios of the lengths of the triangle's sides relative to that acute angle.

Here are the approximate ratios for angle measures $55\degree$, $65\degree$, and $75\degree$.

Angle | $55\degree$ | $65\degree$ | $75\degree$
:-: | :-: | :-: | :-:
$\dfrac{\text{adjacent leg length}}{\text{hypotenuse length}}$ | $0.57$ | $0.42$ | $0.26$
$\dfrac{\text{opposite leg length}}{\text{hypotenuse length}}$ | $0.82$ | $0.91$ | $0.97$
$\dfrac{\text{opposite leg length}}{\text{adjacent leg length}}$ | $1.43$ | $2.14$ | $3.73$
